newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's July tax collection drops vs June-Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: Russia's July tax collection drops vs June-Yeltsin.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin was quoted as saying on Wednesday he was dissatisfied with tax collection in the first half of July which had dropped 20 percent compared to June, Russian news agencies said.
The agencies quoted Yeltsin as saying after meeting Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin at a holiday residence in Karelia that he had approved a tougher approach to major tax debtors.

A list of the 50 biggest corporate non-payers would be drawn by the government. "The conversation with them would be very tough, up to the sacking of managers and closing of the enterprises," Itar-Tass news agency quoted Yeltsin as saying.
"The president considers that taxation services are too liberal towards non-payers," Tass said.

Poor collection of taxes has led to a vicious circle of non-payments which is strangling the Russian economy. Its improvement is crucial for the government's plan to pay off a huge backlog of wages to those on the state payroll by the start of next year.
Up to July, tax collection appeared to be slightly improving, under huge pressure from the reshuffled government powered by youthful reformers.
The state had collected 100 trillion roubles, or 85 percent of planned levels, in the first five months of the year, compared with 69 percent in the first quarter.
In June the government collected 25.8 trillion roubles ($4.46 billion) in tax revenue, or 3.5 percent above the target level, according to a State Tax Service official.
